name: Havilah
title: Descendant of Cush
summary: Havilah is a biblical figure mentioned in Genesis as the son of Cush, grandson of Ham, and great-grandson of Noah. The name Havilah also refers to another person, a son of Joktan, who was a descendant of Shem. The name Havilah is also associated with a land rich in gold, mentioned in connection with the Garden of Eden and in the genealogies after the flood.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Noah's genealogy
keyEvents.description: Havilah is mentioned as one of the sons of Cush, son of Ham, in the post-flood genealogy. He is thus part of the peoples who spread across the earth.

keyEvents.title: The Land of Havilah by the Garden of Eden
keyEvents.description: The land of Havilah is mentioned in connection with the river Pishon that flowed out from the Garden of Eden, and is described as a land rich in gold, bdellium resin, and onyx stone.

keyEvents.title: Havilah as a descendant of Joktan
keyEvents.description: Another Havilah is mentioned as a son of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, showing that the name was linked to several family lines in early biblical history.

keyEvents.title: The Dispersion of the Nations
keyEvents.description: Havilah and his brothers represent the nations that spread out after the flood, according to the table of nations in Genesis chapter 10.

keyEvents.title: Havilah as a geographical boundary marker
keyEvents.description: Havilah is mentioned as a geographical reference in connection with the settlement area of the Ishmaelites, from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt.

keyEvents.title: Saul's War Against the Amalekites
keyEvents.description: Havilah is mentioned as a geographical boundary when King Saul defeated the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which lies east of Egypt.
